common_name: Baby Yellow Nasturtium (AAS-Winning Compact Mounding Yellow Nasturtium)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost, since nasturtiums resent root disturbance and transplant poorly; Baby Yellow stays compact at about 12 inches with dark, contrasting foliage that sets off its clear yellow blooms.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost into lean, well-drained soil in full sun, since nasturtium seedlings resist transplanting well. Baby Yellow is the clear golden-yellow member of the AAS-winning Baby series, its bright, non-fading flowers held upright above dark, contrasting foliage on the same petite, uniformly mounding plant shared by Baby Red and Baby Gold. Its compact 10-to-12-inch scale keeps it tidy in containers, window boxes, and small-space beds where a standard trailing nasturtium would quickly sprawl out of bounds. Both leaves and flowers are edible with a peppery bite; keep the soil lean and skip heavy fertilizer, since rich soil pushes leafy growth at the expense of bloom.

common_name: Baby Red Nasturtium (AAS-Winning Compact Mounding Red Nasturtium)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost, since nasturtiums resent root disturbance and transplant poorly; Baby Red stays compact at about 12 inches with dark, contrasting foliage that sets off its saturated red blooms.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost into lean, well-drained soil in full sun, since nasturtium seedlings resist transplanting well. Baby Red carries the deepest, most saturated flower color of the AAS-winning Baby series, its velvety scarlet-red blooms held upright above dark foliage rather than flopping, on the same petite, uniformly mounding habit shared by Baby Yellow and Baby Gold. Its small 10-to-12-inch scale suits containers, edging, and tight garden pockets where a standard vining nasturtium would take over the bed. Both leaves and flowers are edible with a peppery bite; grow in lean soil without heavy fertilizer, since rich soil favors leafy growth over flowering.

common_name: Baby Gold Nasturtium (AAS-Winning Compact Mounding Gold Nasturtium)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost, since nasturtiums resent root disturbance and transplant poorly; Baby Gold stays compact at about 12 inches with dark, contrasting foliage that sets off its warm gold-orange blooms.

directions: Direct sow after the last frost into lean, well-drained soil in full sun, since nasturtium seedlings resist transplanting well. Baby Gold opens warm, deep gold-orange flowers with a faint apricot cast, a richer tone than the clear yellow of its Baby Yellow series-mate, held upright above dark foliage on the same petite, uniformly mounding plant shared by Baby Yellow and Baby Red. Its compact 10-to-12-inch scale makes it a strong choice for containers, hanging baskets, and small raised beds where a standard sprawling nasturtium would overrun its neighbors. Both leaves and flowers are edible with a peppery bite; keep soil lean and skip heavy fertilizer, since rich soil pushes leafy growth at the expense of bloom.
